title: Fainting
summary: If someone feels faint, have them lie down or tense their leg and arm muscles. If they faint, lay them flat and check breathing – most recover within a minute.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if any of these apply
when: They do not wake within a minute, or are not breathing normally
Fainting with chest pain, palpitations, breathlessness or a severe headache
Fainting during exercise or without warning
They are injured, pregnant, older, or have heart problems

steps.title: Feeling faint
steps.text: Help them sit or lie down. If they can't, cross the legs and tense the leg, buttock and arm muscles (or squat) until the feeling passes.

steps.title: If they faint
steps.text: Lay them flat on their back. Check breathing. If not breathing normally, start CPR.

steps.title: Help recovery
steps.text: Loosen tight clothing and give them fresh air. Raising the legs may help if there is no injury.

steps.title: If they don't wake within a minute
steps.text: Call {EMERGENCY}. Place them in the recovery position if breathing.

steps.title: After they recover
steps.text: Keep them sitting or lying for a while. Check for injuries from the fall. They should get medical advice.

doNot: Do not prop them up in a chair while unconscious
Do not give anything by mouth until fully alert
Do not let them stand up quickly

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)
